name: YJ-21 hypersonic anti-ship missile
overview_md:
The YJ-21 is China's ship- and air-launched hypersonic anti-ship missile — a weapon that brings hypersonic, manoeuvring terminal attack to the fleet and the bomber force rather than only to land-based launchers. It burst into public view in 2022 when the PLA Navy released footage of a YJ-21 being fired from a Type 055 destroyer, and an air-launched version is associated with the H-6 bomber.

Reported performance places it in the anti-ship ballistic/hypersonic class: a boosted missile that descends and manoeuvres in its terminal phase at very high speed — figures cited run to Mach 6 and above — to defeat shipboard defences and strike high-value targets such as carriers. Range estimates vary widely (often cited around 1,000–1,500 km), and as with all such systems the headline numbers should be treated with caution.

For an analyst, the YJ-21's importance is that it puts a hypersonic anti-ship weapon on mobile, survivable platforms — a 12,000-tonne cruiser-sized destroyer and a long-range bomber — rather than only on fixed or land-mobile launchers. That mobility complicates targeting of the launcher and extends the geometry from which a carrier can be threatened, deepening the anti-access problem the U.S. Navy must solve.
builder: China Aerospace Science and Industry Corp. (CASIC)

combat_history.event: PLA Navy released footage of a YJ-21 launched from a Type 055-class destroyer.
combat_history.significance: Public confirmation of a ship-launched hypersonic anti-ship weapon.

modernization.description: Integration across Type 055 destroyers and the bomber force.
modernization.impact: Puts mobile hypersonic anti-ship strike on survivable platforms.

vulnerabilities.description: Range, accuracy and terminal seeker performance are not independently confirmed.
vulnerabilities.context: Open-source figures vary widely; treat as estimates.

vulnerabilities.description: Long-range anti-ship use still relies on detecting and cueing a moving target.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Hypersonic anti-ship strike from Type 055 destroyers and H-6 bombers against high-value naval targets.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Type 055 surface action groups; bomber raids under fighter cover.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: DF-21D is land-launched; the YJ-21 puts a comparable anti-ship hypersonic capability on mobile ships and bombers.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: China takes the carrier-killer to sea.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Zircon is a ship/sub-launched hypersonic cruise missile; the YJ-21 is a boosted manoeuvring anti-ship weapon.
The U.S. relies on subsonic stealthy and dual-role weapons rather than ship-launched hypersonic ASBMs.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: How the US Navy answers the hypersonic anti-ship threat.

doctrine.role: Ship- and air-launched hypersonic anti-ship missile for striking high-value naval targets such as carriers.
doctrine.employment: Fired from Type 055 VLS or H-6 bombers; manoeuvring hypersonic terminal attack to defeat fleet defences.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Put the carrier-killer threat on mobile, survivable platforms.
doctrine.threat_context: Extends China's anti-ship hypersonic threat beyond fixed land launchers, complicating U.S. carrier operations.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the land-based DF-21D and Russia's ship-launched Zircon.
